note: A body that must draw from two chemistries at once needs a boundary between them that stays where it was left. Spatial law is written on this sea, so its coastline is the only line in the setting that does not move; on the plains the salt/fresh line is a claim and on the Widow Run it relocates every settlement on it, and a brackish niche on either ground would be drained or poisoned rather than held.

The run is the only watercourse on the tier that is not brine, and its bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it. This is the only body in the record that can sit out a dry season on pan brine and then drink the flood, so it is the one population that the river's schedule can feed rather than evict - which is why the crossing spread along the trade route and not across open ground.

The saturated floor can only persist on the tier whose three seats are spent on physical, life and qi, because elemental law is left unwritten there and nothing on the plains carries a drying clause. That is also why the most concentrated brine in the setting sits on the least-worked ground: a body specialised past its parent has to go where the resource is, and on this tier the resource is everywhere nobody settled.

Forty years of cutting down to stone that pays nothing left one pit on the plains deep enough to hold a standing sump, and the saltfolk the seam had no further use for are the ones who went down. Above the brine line they stop within hours, so the floor is not a habitat they chose but the last surface the cut produced that a saltfolk body could still occupy.

Neither the colony nor its replacement can survive an open sky, so a subspecies that lost its symbiont did not gain a homeland and lost the only one it had. The folded bedding of this range is the deepest karst in the setting under a frame that writes all six law groups, and saturated air with a strain within range was the parent's condition, inherited here exactly - the two bodies differ in what answers introspection, not in where they can stand.

The mineral bloom took the wound the failed colony left behind, and a bloom needs fresh silicate exposed to nucleate on; this is the one face on the ridge where rock is cut open every day. It is also the only institution in the setting that measures its world instead of praising it, which is why a body whose entire value is as a measured control case was found on the ground that does the measuring.

The two tiers below leave elemental law unspent, so the fire half of this crossing ran at full strength and produced nothing at all. This seam is the first ground where elemental law is written twice, which means the fastest cultivation rate in the record finally has something to spend into - and it is the only reason the whole hybrid crowds onto one rock instead of spreading along a belt that gave them nothing.

Nobody chose this crossing; it happened on the ash-fall end of the same arc, where the ash parent is native and a fire body was already trading, and a shared border produces hybrids nobody planned. The lung scarring is an ash problem and it follows them off the rock unchanged, which is why the belt is not where they came from but the only place the crossing could be afforded to run fast.

This is the only tier whose unwritten elemental law leaves brine standing instead of driving it off, so a saltfolk basin could exist on it at all. When that basin's concentration was changed rather than removed, nothing in the frame intervened - which is the entire difference between this extinction and a hunt, and the reason the record calls it undeclared.

The run's bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it, so each flood recharged the sump with fresh chemistry on a schedule nobody had to decide. Substitution by timetable rather than by event is why this took three declining generations instead of one dying one, and why the last cohort was viable only as long as the old brine survived in a single sealed sump.

Both parents are already on this high ground - the masonry body is worked into the district's load paths and the furnace body is native to it - so the one recorded crossing happened where neither half had to be moved to breed. The ceiling that stops this body at the fourth gate is anatomical rather than jurisdictional: a district with four duplicate imprints cannot create the paired organ set this frame never grew.

This is the only ground in the setting where elemental law is written twice, so a mineral frame carrying a genuine fire circulation stops conducting its heat away and starts fighting its own halves. Below it a stonebound is a warm stone: durable, and dead at sixty, which is the same fact the body was built to survive.

Recorded as a range and not a homeland on purpose, because this body has none: the spore only finishes inside a living host, so the configuration is as widespread as the host species. The commonborn are native to the one tier that seats physical, life and qi and licenses nothing else, which is the only reason a body whose habitat is a person has anywhere at all to be found.

The last unworked iron is the only reason anyone settles ground that cannot be measured, and settlement density is host density. On a tier where distance is not conserved the rarity of this configuration is a function of household count rather than of territory, which is why the pairing is renewed every generation as a household contract and never held as territory.

A life law sitting at the floor of its range still permits a body; what it cannot do is write the form down. There is no slot in which to inscribe one, so this is the residue of an allowance rather than a descendant of anything - an outline with no seat, a form that borrows the qi of whoever supplies the outline, and a copy made by recall rather than by breeding.

A wake is sustained by being misremembered and destroyed by being written down, and the practice that keeps them stable everywhere is a refusal to discuss them at length. This crypt stands in the one place on the plains where a fixed record cannot be kept, which makes it the only ground in the setting where a thing that must not be documented can be left to accumulate without anyone filing it.

The Marshal's authority is over river crossings and the one levy a person may refuse, so a house selling a bed, a hot meal and an acceptable guarantor is priced against the nights the road is shut. A watercourse whose bed moves far enough between floods to relocate every settlement on it is a road its own customers re-survey every season, which is why this culture's real product is sameness: one stew, one price stated at the door, identical at every house between two floods.

The scrub is the only ground on the plains where the one plant that grows is medicine, feed and famine in the same season, and it cannot be fenced around a slow crop. Three locks on a single storehouse and a garment altered being read as a garment whose value was miscounted are the arithmetic of a household whose entire larder is a crop every neighbour is also harvesting, which is why the famine's manners outlived the famine's arithmetic.

This culture's one observance is a counted distribution held on no date, whenever the season turns and the tally can be made honestly. On the plains the flood is the only clock anybody owns and it is written at a law value with qi on the floor, so the date cannot be announced in advance - the culture's refusal to fix a festival is not austerity, it is the only scheduling available to people whose year is a river.

Every mortal-band breakthrough is fought on the one tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one, and the ring survives entirely on spectators, which makes its gate fees the only tax the plains can actually collect. This culture's art is a wall-sized chart of how much of the frame's ceiling was already spent at each person's birth, and this is the one ring where that chart has a subject in front of it.

The reports that matter to this culture are a rhythm heard from under the stair, at a period nobody reproduces, matching the mortal ladder only if time is running at its floor value. An asymptote needs a limit that never arrives and will not stop being true, and this is the one source that supplies one from underneath rather than from a gate nobody can pass.

A grade on a gate is only enforceable where the gate can be scheduled, and this pass can be because the spirit tier writes spatial and temporal law: it is surveyed, closed and reopened on a timetable. That makes it the first ground in the setting where reading a stranger before greeting them is worth doing, because the reading has a consequence that recurs on a date.

A credential is only portable along a road that has a constituency on more than one tier, and this is the setting's first such road and the only piece of the mortal tier with four. Its dialects being four is why this culture keeps one written form for numbers of people and none for anything else: what has to stay identical between tiers is the count of who may cross, not what they are called.

The discipline exists because the mortal frame leaves elemental law unwritten, so a furnace body has no budget to draw on and every discharge is paid in flesh that cannot be repaired. On a tier that seats elemental law there is nothing to quench and the school would have no reason to exist at all, which is why it teaches cold food and naked stone rooms on the one tier that made it necessary.

The practice rooms are built where the ground is cold, and the spent-out face is the only ground on the plains with stone exposed and no ore left to justify fuel burnt to heat it. Spending a body to warm a room that a worked seam would have paid for is the whole argument for building here instead, and the room with no fire at all is the drill.

A house that keeps its real figures in one head and forbids them being written can only operate on ground where a fixed record cannot be kept, and this crypt sits in the one place on the plains where that is true. The site is either the worst possible place for a library or the safest, and this house read it as the safest on purpose.

The register here is not a cipher but a sentence order that makes the listener walk away carrying the market figures instead of the household's. On ground where distance is not conserved and no two surveys of the same place have ever agreed, that is not concealment at all - it is the only description of the terrain that would survive contact with anyone trying to survey it.

Fifteen imprints over three layers leave nine surplus and at this tier the surplus is the place: nothing grows, nothing recovers, nothing is cheap, and access is a discipline rather than a journey. That is why the last hour of the settlement is spent in a queue rather than a shift, and why the ceiling over the floor is left deliberately high - the standing sound needs somewhere to decay, and at this tier nothing is cheap enough to close it.

Not spatial membership but the practice the condition gets: the hum is a transformed reading of the same law value the floor's instruments are running at, which makes this the only place in the setting where a strained law is performed rather than described. A strained law runs and nothing can be done to it, and holding a note through it is the whole labour the culture performs.

The anchorage is the one berth no ledger admits to owning, and this is the only body of water in the setting whose coastline holds its shape. A berth can therefore be added to it without any survey that would have had to record the addition, which is the only reason a community that had made itself impossible to enumerate still has a harbour to be impossible in.

A community whose entire discipline is that nothing written is nothing owed can still run a schedule it never has to keep, because the anchored season is announced by the sea itself. That is the one timetable available to a people that has refused every other record, and the refusal is only affordable because the sea continues to publish its dates to nobody in particular.

A hull's marking is this culture's only legal statement and every other port reads it as a promise of honesty, which only carries weight if the port doing the reading is still in the same place. This is the one sea whose coastline holds its shape and whose tide keeps time, and that stability is the entire reason a people that abandoned its price list four centuries ago was still here to be raided - it never was, because it never priced the cargo.

Spirit stone and jade ore in one bedding is the reason a Void Serpent was worth more than the ship carrying it: the cargo and the ground it came out of are the same accident, so every claim on the stone is a claim on the serpent. Declining to price the cargo is what made the ridge's owners leave this community alone, and it is the single decision that has kept the settlement inhabited.

The office sells standing on the one graded route out of the plains, and a seat there cannot be mortared because the crossing's upkeep is charged per period and nobody who ever attempted it could pay. What it holds is therefore a bed rather than a crossing - a stretch of unmortared ground sold one place at a time - which is the difference between holding the border and selling a position on it.

On ground where distance is not conserved and no two surveys have ever agreed, no office can produce evidence that it held the crossing, so the bed has no stability and only a price. Every assumption that somebody is holding it is somebody else's problem, and the terrain is what makes the office unanswerable rather than the accounting.

The isle was cut out of this sea's floor when a jade seam was worked out from under it and resealed at drifted readings, so nothing on it can be appraised against its parent. That is the whole business in one fact: low-grade jade is worthless on the isle and unmatchable ashore, and a severed frame is the only ground in the setting where a network whose chief asset is that its members are on no list can hold stock nobody is able to value.

The residue is sold as spirit stone and this is the only face in the setting where spirit stone is cut, and its yield has been falling for three generations. A falling answer is the entire reason low-grade tailings have a buyer at all, and it is also why the charter holder takes a share of the value rather than the material - the isle's supply is somebody else's uncollected obligation, so two sellers of the same tailings would make the claim read as invented.

The society's entire capital is hours spent being seen once a year and it keeps no register at all, which only works if the date arrives without anyone recording it. Temporal law is written on this sea, so the tide names the re-drawing for free and the community is never obliged to keep the one piece of paper its own rules forbid.

At the turn of the shelf's own tide the water stops moving and everything in it has to decide, and that is precisely what an unsettled claim does once a year: carried by two holders, neither told what the other holds, discharged in public and never afterwards contestable. A holding here is a place somebody can hold rather than a place the creature is, which is the only form of security this society can offer.

A lodge with no roster, no rate and no address can only be found at a door that already has one, and this is the single stretch where a rift has stood open long enough to be a door rather than a scar. It closes when the value returns in range, so the shore is a door with a timetable - and a lodge that keeps no record of its customers has to trade on someone else's schedule.

A boundary here is not a wall between neighbours but the edge of a law budget, so a body arriving where a group it relied on is unwritten is injured rather than slowed. The lodge sells the only scarce thing at a crossing, which is a person the far side will not reject, and it can only do that from the edge - spending other people's visibility on the near side as the capital that makes the sale possible.
